input.command: ls -la; cat -n src/routes.ts; ls src; cat CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null
input.description: List repo files and show routes source and CLAUDE.md

input.command: cat -n src/worktree.ts; cat -n src/store.ts; cat -n src/config.ts; cat package.json
cat -n src/api.ts; cat -n src/git-auth.ts; grep -rn "params\|cachePath\|REPOS_DIR\|registerRepo\|template\|cacheListing" src
input.description: Show api wiring and search route usages

input.reason: I read src/routes.ts, src/worktree.ts, src/store.ts, src/config.ts and src/git-auth.ts. registerRepo (routes.ts:19-22) checks only that id and remoteUrl are non-empty. It then stores the id and clones into cachePath(id), which is path.resolve(REPOS_DIR, id) (worktree.ts:10). The template route builds its base with path.join(REPOS_DIR, req.params.id) (routes.ts:36). Its startsWith check (routes.ts:38) only compares the file against that base, so it cannot stop the base itself from escaping. cacheListing uses cachePath(req.params.id) (routes.ts:60). No validation exists anywhere in the repository. `../../etc` escapes on both routes. An absolute id escapes only on the cache listing route, because path.join treats `/etc` as a relative segment and produces /var/harbor/repos/etc. There is no CLAUDE.md in the working tree, so F14's invariant citation is unsupported. Its factual claim about line 36 still holds.
input.summary: Unvalidated repository ids let routes escape the repositories directory

findings.text: The repository id is stored with no character or path validation and later used as a directory name. An id such as `../../etc` escapes the repositories directory on both the template route and the cache listing route; an absolute path such as `/etc` escapes it on the cache listing route.
findings.reason: Most of the finding holds. registerRepo only checks that id is non-empty (routes.ts:20), stores it (routes.ts:21), and passes it to cloneRepo, which uses cachePath(id) as the clone directory (worktree.ts:14-15). `../../etc` escapes on both routes: path.join gives /var/harbor/repos/../../etc = /var/etc on the template route, and path.resolve gives /var/etc on the cache listing route. Because the startsWith guard compares against the already-escaped base, it passes. The absolute-path part is wrong for the template route. path.join does not reset on an absolute segment, so `/etc` becomes /var/harbor/repos/etc and stays inside the directory. Only cachePath's path.resolve turns `/etc` into /etc. The clause is narrowed to the cache listing route.

findings.text: The template route builds its base directory from the raw repository id.
findings.reason: The first sentence holds. Line 36 joins REPOS_DIR with req.params.id and never validates it. The only guard, at line 38, checks the file against that same unvalidated base. The second sentence depends on CLAUDE.md, which is not in the working tree (the repository root holds only package.json and src/). The claimed invariant has no support in the code, so that sentence is removed.

input.severity_reason: The template route has no authentication or authorization check. With id `../../..` the base becomes `/`, and a name such as `../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd, which still passes the startsWith(base) check. That gives arbitrary file read. cacheListing can also read INDEX files anywhere, and registerRepo can git-clone into any writable path. This is an exploitable security flaw.
